Ran 49 commands, read memory
The heading bug was systemic. Any Text without an explicit style inherited Material 3’s bodyLarge, which has a fixed 24sp line height. Your Nord uses the default 40sp heading size, so wrapped lines got 24sp of spacing and collided. bodyLarge now uses the font’s natural line height, which fixes every oversized label in the app, not just Moon Illumination.

Phase 9c: clock widgets without the per-second foreground service

The widgets now use the system AnalogClock, and the launcher ticks the hands, including the seconds hand.
The app draws the hands once in your chosen needle skin and accent colour. The sweeping trail is built into the second hand.
The date is a TextClock, so it rolls over at midnight on its own.
The day/night icon refreshes from an alarm at 6:00 and 19:00 that doesn’t wake the phone. It now uses the same 6–18 daytime range as the clock panel.
Widgets refresh when you leave the app, so skin and accent changes show up.
Upgraded installs also cancel the old one-minute alarm.
The foreground service, notification, battery-optimisation setup screen and their 6 strings in all 14 languages are gone. So are the FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_SPECIAL_USE and POST_NOTIFICATIONS permissions, which nothing else used.
The 3x3 widget was using the 4x4 layout; that’s fixed.
A new DayNightTest covers the day/night boundaries.
Unused helper functions in BitmapHelper and PermissionUtils were removed, and the accent-to-theme lookup moved to AccentThemes, shared by activities and widgets.
Trade-offs to know about:

Android 12+ only: The clock widgets need Android 12 or newer, because that’s when the system clock gained custom hands. On older Android they are hidden; everything else still supports Android 7+.
12-hour face: The clock widgets always use the 12-hour face, because the system clock can’t turn an hour hand on a 24-hour dial.
The README is updated: Phase 9c is done, and Phase 10 (the OpenStreetMap fallback) is next.

Phase 10a is done: the GPS panel can now show OpenStreetMap instead of Google Maps. Nothing here has been compiled or run, because the Android SDK and Maven repositories aren’t reachable from my sandbox. CI is the first real check.

The tarball builds on top of master and also contains the Phase 9c changes from my last reply, since your repo doesn’t have them yet. Extracting it again is harmless if you’ve already applied 9c.

Download: /mnt/user-data/outputs/positional-phase10a.tar.gz (52 changed or added files; extract at the repo root)

Delete (same list as 9c; skip if you already ran it):

sh
git rm app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/activities/service/ClockWidgetActivity.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/model/ClockModel.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/services/ClockWidgetService.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/services/ClockWidgetService2x2.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/services/ClockWidgetService3x3.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/services/ClockWidgetService4x4.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/widgets/ClockWidget2x2.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/widgets/ClockWidget3x3.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/widgets/ClockWidget4x4.java app/src/main/res/drawable/ic_place_notification.xml
What’s new

Map source setting: Settings now has Automatic, Google Maps and OpenStreetMap. Automatic picks OpenStreetMap when the build has no MAPS_API_KEY and Google Maps otherwise.
No automatic quota fallback: Google’s map library gives no signal when a key is rejected or over quota, so the app can’t switch on its own. If the Google map stays blank, pick OpenStreetMap.
Map library: The OpenStreetMap view uses MapLibre Native 13.7.1 (OpenGL build), which is actively maintained. I didn’t use osmdroid because it was archived in 2024.
Tile cache: Map tiles are cached on the device, up to 128 MB.
Night mode: Map tiles are darkened in night mode.
Same GPS features: The pin, accuracy circle, target line, follow mode, and compass and bearing rotation all work on OpenStreetMap.
Shared code: The GPS panel now talks to a GpsMap interface with a Google and an OpenStreetMap version, and the pin drawing is shared between them.
Tests: New unit tests cover the map source choice, the map style, and the accuracy circle radius.
Trade-offs

Bigger APK: MapLibre adds native code. To limit the size, the APK now includes only arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64, so 32-bit x86 emulators can no longer install it.
Google-only options: Satellite, labels, traffic, buildings and high contrast do nothing on OpenStreetMap.
Not migrated yet: The trail and measure panels and map search still use Google Maps. They are Phase 10b and 10c.
Docs updated

The README phase table now shows 10a done and 10b next.
PRIVACY.md, the privacy, terms, internet-use and credits pages now mention that OpenStreetMap’s tile servers see your IP address and the area you view.
The credits page also had two stale entries (Timeline-View and Material Components, both removed in earlier phases); those are fixed.

Phase 10b is done: the trail and measure panels can now show OpenStreetMap too, so the map source setting covers the GPS, trail and measure panels. This tarball is cumulative and includes the 9c and 10a changes, since your master still has neither.

None of 9c, 10a or 10b has been compiled. I can’t reach Maven or the Android SDK from here, so the next CI run is the first real check, and three phases of untested code are now stacked.

Download: /mnt/user-data/outputs/positional-phase10b.tar.gz (61 changed or added files; extract at the repo root)

Delete (unchanged from 9c; skip if you already ran it):

sh
git rm app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/activities/service/ClockWidgetActivity.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/model/ClockModel.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/services/ClockWidgetService.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/services/ClockWidgetService2x2.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/services/ClockWidgetService3x3.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/services/ClockWidgetService4x4.kt app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/widgets/ClockWidget2x2.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/widgets/ClockWidget3x3.java app/src/main/java/app/simple/positional/widgets/ClockWidget4x4.java app/src/main/res/drawable/ic_place_notification.xml
What changed in 10b

Shared map base: A new OsmMapView holds everything the three OpenStreetMap maps have in common: the camera, the compass sensor, the location pin, the accuracy circle, lines, and fitting the view to all points. The 10a GPS map was rebuilt on it.
Panels behind interfaces: The trail and measure panels now talk to TrailMap and MeasureMap interfaces, with one Google version and one OpenStreetMap version of each. The panels themselves no longer care which map is underneath.
Trail on OpenStreetMap: You get the trail line, a marker icon for each saved point, wrap-to-fit and unwrap, auto-center, and the compass or bearing location pin with its accuracy circle.
Measure on OpenStreetMap: You get the measured line, a dashed guide line from the last point to the screen centre, live distance to the centre, adding and removing points, and wrap-to-fit.
Shared pin logic: The rule that picks the location pin icon (from compass accuracy or movement) is now in one place, used by both the Google and OpenStreetMap maps.
Fixes

Battery drain: The Google trail map’s auto-center timer re-posted itself forever, even after you left the panel. The OpenStreetMap version stops it when the panel is paused.
Dead code: An unused text-label overlay was removed from the Google measure map.
Settings note: The map source note in Settings now names the GPS, trail and measure panels.
Limits on OpenStreetMap: The geodesic trail option and the Google-only map options (satellite, labels, traffic, buildings, high contrast) have no effect there. Map search still uses Google Maps; that’s Phase 10c, now marked Next in the README.

New unit tests cover the location pin choice and the trail markers and line data; the README phase table is updated.
